messages.author: 5a8bfcb87fd22c3b
messages.subject: VB memory usage issue
parts:
Hello,

I've been working with a relatively simple categorical model in Stan, but due to its size I've been using variational inference through vb. The inference seems to complete: it gets to the "returning 1000 approximate samples from the posterior" stage and then prints "COMPLETED." However, before control is returned back to me, memory usage spikes to using all available system memory and effectively hangs my system.

What I'm wondering is: what is happening in this stage and is there any way to deal with the memory spike through some parameters? Can someone who knows the inner workings of the vb call explain what it's doing after ostensibly finishing sampling from the posterior that would cause such a massive consumption of memory?

Thanks,
Rick

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: VB memory usage issue
parts:
On Friday, May 13, 2016 at 2:11:24 PM UTC-4, ricka...@gmail.com wrote:
What I'm wondering is: what is happening in this stage and is there any way to deal with the memory spike through some parameters? Can someone who knows the inner workings of the vb call explain what it's doing after ostensibly finishing sampling from the posterior that would cause such a massive consumption of memory?

My guess is that you have lots of parameters and reading the giant csv file consumes a lot of memory. There are more efficient csv readers out there these days (read_csv() in readr, fread() in data.table) that may work better on the csv file that is (or was) sitting in your temporary directory.

Ben
